title: Prices doubled every 15 hours: Hungary, 1946
head: Prices doubled
every 15 hours.
tag: Full video: the entire history of inflation

thumb.small: Hungary, July 1946: the worst inflation on record

description:
In July 1946, by Hanke and Krus's figures (World Hyperinflations, Cato Working Paper 8), Hungarian prices rose 41.9 quadrillion percent in one month: about 207% a day, doubling every 15 hours. Hungary issued the highest denomination banknote ever, 100 quintillion pengő, and on 1 August 1946 the forint replaced it at 400 octillion pengő. The note on screen is a drawn diagram, not a reproduction. From the full video on Money, Entirely. #inflation #history #economics

title: A kilo of bread: 69,000 marks to 200 billion in three months
head: A kilo of bread, 1923:
69,000 to 200 billion marks
tag: Full video: the entire history of inflation
description:
Germany, October 1923: prices rose 29,500% in a month, about 21% a day, doubling every 3.7 days (Hanke and Krus). The Deutsches Historisches Museum gives a kilo of bread at about 69,000 marks in August 1923 and over 200 billion in November: nearly three million times as much. In November 1923 one US dollar cost 4.2 trillion marks (Deutscher Bundestag). From the full video on Money, Entirely. #inflation #history #economics

title: Prices stopped falling. When did they last fall?
head: Prices used to fall.
Then they stopped.
tag: Full video: the entire history of inflation
description:
In the US consumer price index, the last time prices were lower one December than the December before was 1954 (FRED CPI-U, computed). In the Bank of England's English and UK series, the last yearly fall was 1933; before 1900, prices fell in almost half of all years. $100 of 1913 prices cost about $3,415 in October 2026.
